offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

proposed.why: The evidence is sufficient: the ledger consumer restarted in naive mode and booked a redelivered event twice.

diagnosis.hypothesis: ledger-consumer was restarted at 01:50:43 with its handler changed from idempotent (started 01:49:23) to naive. The naive handler skips the processed_events dedupe insert and books every delivery. The provider re-sent evt_000272 about 0.5 s after the first delivery, and the receiver queued both copies (offsets 123 and 124). The first copy was posted by the idempotent path. The second was posted by the naive path, which made two transactions (272 and 276) for pay_000247. The ledger is therefore $104.44 ahead of the provider, so posted_exactly_once and matches_provider fail. Payments and refunds still match the provider. The confirmer correctly reported already_confirmed both times. The change of mode comes from the startup log only, because recent_deploys failed, so I did not see the deploy record or its settings.

evidence.shows: The money check confirms the symptom: evt_000272 (pay_000247, $104.44) was posted twice, in transactions 272 and 276. The ledger is +$104.44 against the provider. The ledger is still balanced, and payments and refunds match.
ledger-consumer logged posted for evt_000272 twice, from Kafka offsets 123 and 124, at 01:50:42.575 and 01:50:43.254.
recent_deploys failed because Docker did not answer, so the deploy record and the LEDGER_HANDLER setting were not seen.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000272 twice, at offsets 123 and 124. This looks like a normal provider resend, so the receiver is not at fault.
First delivery: the ledger consumer inserted into processed_events, then posted. This is the idempotent path.

Second delivery: the ledger consumer went straight to INSERT transactions and entries, with no processed_events insert, and the outcome was posted. The dedupe was not applied. The confirmer treated the same delivery as already_confirmed.
ledger-consumer started in mode idempotent at 01:49:23 and again in mode naive at 01:50:43, just before the duplicate was booked.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its previous settings (LEDGER_HANDLER=idempotent) so duplicate deliveries are deduped again. Then repair the ledger separately: reverse duplicate transaction 276 for evt_000272, and check whether any other events were posted more than once since 01:50:43. The rollback does not repair money already booked wrong.

The duplicate $104.44 stays in the ledger until it is repaired. The rollback is planned from the deploy log, and code refuses it if there is nothing to undo.
